environment.description: Same Go microservice on EC2, but origin is fronted by CloudFront distribution with OAC-style custom header verification. The origin's security group restricts inbound to CloudFront managed prefix list (com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing) only. CloudFront distribution has a custom origin header X-Origin-Verify set to a 64-char rotating secret validated by an ALB listener rule that returns 403 for requests missing the header match. CloudFront behaviors: /config/update and /admin paths have NO cache behavior defined (returns 403 via CloudFront Function that rejects non-GET methods and paths matching /config/update or /admin). Only /config GET with valid CloudFront signed URL (RSA-SHA1, key group KG-7f2a9b, TTL 300s) passes through. The CloudFront Function (CF2 runtime) inspects request.method and request.uri, returning 403 for POST methods or URIs containing 'update' or 'admin' substring regardless of signing status.

config.network: SG inbound restricted to com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing prefix list
config.origin_header: X-Origin-Verify with 64-char rotating secret, ALB rule validates
config.cloudfront_function: viewer-request stage, blocks POST method and URIs containing 'update' or 'admin'
config.signed_urls: RSA-SHA1 signed URLs required, key group KG-7f2a9b, 300s TTL
config.cache_behaviors: Only /config GET has a defined behavior with signed URL requirement
